title: Data Representation
author: oA7a2DXCeN3DLamvj
chapter_outcomes: Understand binary magnitudes and the difference between binary prefixes and decimal prefixes: kibi and kilo, mebi and mega, gibi and giga, tebi and tera
Convert an integer value from one number base/representation to another
Perform binary addition and subtraction using positive and negative binary integers
Describe practical applications where Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) and Hexadecimal are used

Understand and be able to represent character data in its internal binary form, depending on the character set used; ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange), extended ASCII and Unicode
Understanding how data for a bitmapped image are encoded
Perform calculations to estimate the file size for a bitmap image
Understand the effects of changing elements of a bitmap image on the image quality and file size
Understand how data for a vector graphic are encoded
Justify the use of a bitmap image or a vector graphic for a given task
Understand how sound is represented and encoded
Understand the impact of changing the sampling rate and resolution
Understand the need for and examples of the use of compression
Understand lossy and lossless compression and justify the use of a method in a given situation
Understand how a text file, bitmap image, vector graphic and sound file can be compressed
